examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
examples.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={e}^{x}\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2}-{e}^{0} \\  & ={e}^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
